Download a File With Diagnostic Error Messages

Source: R/lib_data_loader.R
fdl.Rd

Downloads one file like dldata(), but never stops on a network failure: it returns TRUE or FALSE, prints plain-language advice for the usual academic and corporate network problems, and then tries a Wayback Machine copy of the same address. Use it in scripts that other people run on networks you do not control (university VPNs, corporate proxies), where a bare “cannot open the connection” is not enough to act on.

Usage

fdl(url, tpath, attwb = NULL, allowfile = FALSE)

Arguments

url

URL to download, a single string.

tpath

Destination path on disk, a single string.

attwb

The Wayback Machine snapshot URL tried as a fallback if the primary download fails. NULL (the default) resolves a snapshot automatically via wbsnpurl() (one more request); a URL string overrides the lookup; "" or FALSE disables the fallback entirely.

allowfile

Logical. Accept a file:// URL for url (default FALSE; offline tests pass TRUE). It does not apply to attwb.

Value

TRUE if either the primary download or the Wayback fallback succeeded (the file is at tpath), otherwise FALSE.

Details

The URL is checked first, as in dldata(); a refused URL is an error, not FALSE. The download is then attempted. On failure the messages name the URL and the error, then the likely causes picked out from the error text: rate limiting (HTTP 429, common behind shared VPN addresses), a TLS handshake failure (VPNs that inspect TLS, such as Cisco AnyConnect, GlobalProtect, Zscaler or Netskope), a DNS failure, a refused or reset connection, a timeout, an HTTP 403, or otherwise a moved file or a portal that is down. When base R reports the HTTP status only in a warning, that warning's text is used as the cause.

The fallback: with attwb = NULL a snapshot is looked up with wbsnpurl(); with a URL that URL is used; with "" or FALSE the fallback is off. The fallback is fetched without allowfile, so it must be a public https URL even when allowfile = TRUE; a refused fallback URL counts as a failed fallback (FALSE), with a message.

All output goes to the message stream. The transport always draws its progress (it is called with quiet = FALSE). tpath is overwritten on success.

Examples

src <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
writeLines(c("id,value", "1,10"), src)

# a successful download returns TRUE
fdl(paste0("file://", src), tempfile(fileext = ".csv"),
  attwb = "", allowfile = TRUE)
#> [1] TRUE

# a failed one returns FALSE with advice, here with the fallback off
fdl(paste0("file://", src, "-missing"), tempfile(),
  attwb = "", allowfile = TRUE)
#>   ! Download failed.
#>     URL:   file:///tmp/RtmpItpcMj/file1fbb6c0f1322.csv-missing
#>     Error: cannot open file '/tmp/RtmpItpcMj/file1fbb6c0f1322.csv-missing': No such file or directory
#> 
#>   Common causes (in rough order of likelihood):
#>     * The server did not serve the file (see the error above): the URL may have moved or the
#>       portal may be down.
#>   The Wayback fallback is switched off; nothing more to try.
#> [1] FALSE

# a refused URL is an error, not FALSE
try(fdl("http://example.org/data.csv", tempfile()))
#> Error : url must be an https:// URL, not http:// ('http://example.org/data.csv'); options(rmoriebricklayer.allowhttp = TRUE) admits a trusted plain-http mirror

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# needs the network; the Wayback fallback is looked up on failure
ok <- fdl("https://cloud.r-project.org/",
  tempfile(fileext = ".html"))
ok
}
